conventions.convention: An assigned sharp observable is a densely defined self-adjoint operator together with its declared spectral-coordinate unit; its domain is part of the assignment.
Outcome laws are Borel probability measures: μρA(B)=tr(ρ EA(B)); a pure preparation is evaluated using a unit representative. Zero singleton probability does not exclude point realizations.

For a unit vector, finite absolute first moment is equivalent to membership in D(|A|½), whereas finite second moment is equivalent to membership in D(A). The A² quadratic-form variance formula additionally requires D(A²).
Zero-weight terms are omitted before evaluating component integrals or undefined component means. Mixed-state moment criteria require weighted summability, not merely component domain membership.
The Plancherel transform uses exp(−2πi x·ξ), so the momentum multiplier is 2πℏ ξj and the one-coordinate momentum density includes the Jacobian factor (2πℏ)⁻¹.
The spectral construction explicitly assumes AC and countable choice; the mathematical affinity result assumes countable choice with the spectral PVM supplied as data.

load_bearing.statement: Under P1, P2, AC and countable choice, an assigned sharp observable (A,uA) has its self-adjoint domain and spectral PVM specified; its preparation-dependent outcome law is μρA(B)=tr(ρ EA(B)), equal to ‖EA(B)ψ‖² for a unit pure preparation.

Under AC and countable choice, for self-adjoint A on a nonzero complex Hilbert space and unit ψ, the second spectral moment is finite exactly on D(A), with value ‖Aψ‖²; the absolute first moment is finite exactly on D(|A|½). On D(A), the mean is ⟨Aψ,ψ⟩ and variance is ‖(A−⟨Aψ,ψ⟩)ψ‖². Density-operator moments are the weighted component integrals, using the explicit zero-weight convention and weighted summability criteria.

Under AC and countable choice, EA({λ}) is the orthogonal projection onto {x∈D(A):Ax=λx}; it is nonzero exactly when λ is an eigenvalue. Non-eigenvalues have zero singleton probability in every density operator, and a unit eigenvector has singleton probability one.
With countable choice and a supplied spectral PVM, trace-norm mixtures satisfy μΣwnρnA(B)=Σwn μρnA(B), and supB |μρA(B)−μσA(B)|≤‖ρ−σ‖₁.

Under P2, the spinless massive-particle model P5, AC and countable choice, position spectral projections are indicator multipliers, the joint position density is |ψ|² or Σwn|un|², and momentum projections are Fourier-transported indicator multipliers for 2πℏ ξj. Coordinate laws are absolutely continuous and atomless; their spectra are R.

Distinct density operators on a nonzero complex Hilbert space are separated by some unit-vector quadratic form and hence by the singleton law at 1 of the rank-one projection Tww; its probability difference is bounded by their trace-norm distance.

concerns.concern: Counterexample step 1.2, lines 97–99, has corrupted mathematical notation: 'eta_n(x):=prod_{j=1}^3max{0,1-n|x_j-X_j|}', '|eta_n|_2le(2/n)^{3/2}', and '1=|int feta_n|le|f|_2(2/n)^{3/2}'. The rho symbol is split into a newline followed by 'ho'. These are not the defined symbols or valid expressions as printed. The intended tent-function/Cauchy–Schwarz proof is recoverable and sound, but the carrier needs notation restoration.

Proof steps 1.1–1.2 apply the product-measurable Tonelli supplier directly to arbitrary Lebesgue-measurable L² representatives and their null-set modifications. The proof starts on '(R³, Borel, Lebesgue)' but does not explicitly select Borel representatives or explain passage to the completed Lebesgue spaces and almost-everywhere sections. The conclusions are correct; a brief representative/completion argument is needed to match the cited theorem's actual product-measurability hypothesis.

The physical_scope describes 'pure-preparation laws of density |ψ-hat|² in the momentum variable', while the Statement defines the transform using frequency ξ and correctly includes p=2πℏξ and its Jacobian in clause (c). With that explicitly fixed transform, |F₂ψ|² is a frequency density, not the unscaled momentum density. The scope wording should preserve the normalization already present in the Statement; the scope remark repeats the same shorthand.

alerts.finding: Definition (c), lines 98–100, says 'a mean exists exactly when ρ is concentrated on the domain of |A|^{1/2} in the sense of those items'. Neither cited batch-45 moment item defines this concentration condition; both require a finite weighted sum of absolute first moments. Domain membership alone is insufficient: on ℓ² take A en=n en and ρ=Σn≥1 c n⁻² Tenen, with c normalizing the weights. Every en lies in D(A), and even ran(ρ)⊆D(A), but the absolute first moment is cΣn≥1 n⁻¹=∞. The claimed iff needs the actual weighted integrability criterion.

Definition (e) cites def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law (b) for 'the position density of that preparation as |ψ|²'. That clause supplies only the general scalar spectral law, not the position multiplication PVM or its spatial density. The batch-45 position/momentum theorem (b), or the cited spin-zero kinematics extension, is the relevant supplier. The formula itself is correct.

Definition (d) reads the energy law of a unit eigenstate 'through clause (a)' of def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law as a point mass, then gives position density |ψ|² 'by clause (b)'. Clause (a) defines an assigned observable; the eigenstate singleton law is clause (c) and the atom lemma. Clause (b) is the generic spectral law and does not compute the one-dimensional position density. The claims need their actual atom and multiplication-PVM suppliers.
